Hi Samantha / Carlos —

Thanks for the time earlier — good overview of your use case (real-time grammar suggestions at ~20–40 tokens per request, bursty traffic during peak editing sessions). Quick recap + open items so we have alignment: 

- Recap: you’re focused on tail latency (p99) for the editor UX and want predictable throughput during peak collaboration periods.
- Lingua target: p99 sub-200ms at 20 token output for 95% of active users; some users need <150ms.
- You asked about: (1) our p95 vs p99 tradeoffs with batching, (2) how we’d run a short bench/POC and measurement plan, (3) data controls for private deployments.

Next steps we suggested on the call: 
- Dev-led bench: 48–72 hour POC measuring p50/p95/p99 across a 1:1 and 4:1 batch profile.
- Redwood to share an initial perf note + a sample POC plan (what we’ll measure, what infra we use).
- Procurement touchpoint once POC confirms numbers.

Can you confirm: (a) whether this remains a priority for Q2, and (b) who on your side should be looped for the POC (engineering lead + procurement contact)?

I’ve looped Dev (cc) who will provide a short technical note and an initial p99 reference.

Samantha / Carlos —

Following up with the bench plan and an initial p99 reference. Attaching a short p99 report we run internally (redwood_p99-report.pdf) — this is a 3-day profile showing p50/p95/p99 for a comparable transformer microservice at 20 tokens output. Key notes: 

- Default approach: continuous micro-batching with 8ms scheduling overhead and KV prefix cache for short-history edits.
- p95 is mostly solved by batching; p99 is sensitive to scheduling jitter and long-tail host busy events.
- For Lingua’s profile we recommend a 2-node configuration for the POC with autoscale thresholds at 60% GPU util to avoid tail spikes.

Proposed POC measurement plan (short):
1) Baseline capture of current client profile (you provide sampled traces for 6 hours).
2) 48-hour POC: inject production-like traffic (3–6 concurrent per doc, 1.2k peak) and measure p50/p95/p99 and per-route tokens.
3) Run 3 failure scenarios: (a) cold-cache, (b) simulated host preemption, (c) mixed-batch heavy requests.

I’ll hold a 30-minute office hour on the POC plan if useful — options: May 26 10:00–10:30 PT or May 27 15:00–15:30 PT.

Attachments: redwood_p99-report.pdf

Regards,
Dev Patel
